content.rendered:
If you are having a mental health crisis or need help after regular school hours, the following resources are available for support.

  • If you or someone near you is facing a life threatening emergency, call 911.
  • Washington County 24 hour Crisis Line: 503-291-9111
  • Washington County 24 hour Crisis Line-Hearing Impaired TDD: 1-800-735-2900
  • Hawthorne Walk In Clinic: 503-291-9111
    • Mental health urgent care center for mental health and addiction concerns. Services include assessment, crisis counseling, education, and connection to treatment providers and other social services. Is open to the public during limited hours. Please call ahead to 503-291-9111 to discuss options for assistance and to confirm hours of operation. The center is located at 5240 NE Elam Young Parkway, Suite 100, Hillsboro, OR 97124.
  • Trevor Project for LGBTQ Youth: 866-488-7386
  • YouthLine: 1-877-968-8491 or text teen2teen to 839863.
  • Behavioral Health Support Line: 800-923-4357
    • Offers immediate no-cost behavioral health screening, counseling services, and referrals to mental health and substance use recovery providers.

Sherwood School District Mental Health Support Contacts

  • Chelsie Vukovich, LCSW
  • Behavior and Mental Health Coordinator
  • Phone 503-825-5034
  • cvukovich@sherwood.k12.or.us
  • Mary Massey, LMFT
  • Mental Health Specialist, Sherwood Middle School
  • Suicide Prevention Coordinator
  • Phone 503-825-5645
  • mmassey@sherwood.k12.or.us
  • Eddie Carillo, LPC
  • Mental Health Specialist, Sherwood High School
  • Drug & Alcohol Prevention Coordinator
  • Phone 503-825-6029
  • ecarrillo@sherwood.k12.or.us


Sherwood School District Mental Health Specialists are available to assist students and families who have questions or concerns about mental health and can, when appropriate, assist in finding appropriate treatment and support.

Suicide Prevention

If you are having thoughts of suicide, are suffering from hopelessness, or feel like you can’t cope right now, help is available 24/7. You are not alone. Call the Washington County Crisis Line at 503-291-9111. Language interpreters are available.
